name: Major depressive disorder
overview: A mood disorder characterized by persistent low mood and/or loss of interest or pleasure, together with cognitive and somatic symptoms, causing significant functional impairment. Neuroimaging and electrophysiology research has repeatedly implicated limbic and prefrontal systems, though findings across studies are heterogeneous.

name: Post-traumatic stress disorder
overview: A trauma- and stressor-related disorder that can develop after exposure to actual or threatened death, serious injury, or violence, characterized by intrusive re-experiencing, avoidance, negative alterations in cognition and mood, and hyperarousal. Research has focused on fear-processing and threat-regulation circuitry, with mixed and evolving findings.

name: Schizophrenia
overview: A psychotic disorder characterized by positive symptoms (hallucinations, delusions, disorganized thought), negative symptoms (avolition, blunted affect), and cognitive impairment. It is studied across structural, functional, and electrophysiological modalities, with widespread and heterogeneous findings rather than a single localized alteration.

name: Alzheimer's disease
overview: A progressive neurodegenerative disease and the most common cause of dementia, typically presenting with early episodic memory impairment. Its defining neuropathology is the accumulation of amyloid-beta plaques and tau neurofibrillary tangles, accompanied by progressive atrophy that is studied extensively with structural imaging and PET.

name: Bipolar disorder
overview: A mood disorder characterized by episodes of mania or hypomania, typically alternating with depressive episodes. Neuroimaging research has repeatedly examined fronto-limbic emotion-regulation circuitry, with heterogeneous findings across illness phases and medication states.

name: Generalized anxiety disorder
overview: An anxiety disorder characterized by excessive, difficult-to-control worry across multiple domains, with somatic tension and hyperarousal. Research has focused on threat-processing and emotion-regulation circuitry; the imaging literature is smaller and more mixed than for depression.

name: Obsessive-compulsive disorder
overview: A disorder characterized by intrusive obsessions and repetitive compulsions. Cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical circuitry is the dominant framework in its neuroimaging literature, studied across structural, functional, and stimulation modalities.

name: Dissociative identity disorder
overview: A dissociative disorder involving two or more distinct personality states and recurrent gaps in recall, strongly associated with early-life trauma. Formerly called multiple personality disorder. Its neuroimaging literature is small, based on modest samples, and scientifically contested — indexed evidence here is correspondingly limited.

name: Huntington's disease
overview: An autosomal-dominant neurodegenerative disease caused by a CAG-repeat expansion in the huntingtin gene, presenting with chorea, cognitive decline, and psychiatric symptoms. Progressive striatal degeneration is its pathological hallmark, and striatal atrophy is measurable years before motor onset.

name: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder
overview: A neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by developmentally inappropriate inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity. Neuroimaging and electrophysiology research spans fronto-striatal circuitry and oscillatory markers, with effect sizes that are typically small at the group level.

name: Panic disorder
overview: An anxiety disorder characterized by recurrent unexpected panic attacks and persistent concern about further attacks. Research has focused on fear-circuitry and interoceptive processing; its dedicated neuroimaging literature is smaller than that of depression or PTSD.

name: Anorexia nervosa
overview: An eating disorder characterized by restriction of energy intake, significantly low body weight, intense fear of weight gain, and disturbed body image. Neuroimaging findings are complicated by the confound of starvation state, which itself alters brain structure.

name: Substance use disorders
overview: A group of disorders characterized by compulsive substance use despite harmful consequences. Reward, salience, and executive-control circuitry are the dominant frameworks in the imaging literature, with findings varying substantially by substance.

name: Autism spectrum disorder
overview: A neurodevelopmental condition characterized by differences in social communication together with restricted, repetitive behaviors and interests. Neuroimaging findings are notably heterogeneous, with age- and subgroup-dependent patterns rather than a single consistent signature.

name: Frontotemporal dementia
overview: A group of neurodegenerative disorders with progressive degeneration of frontal and temporal lobes, presenting as behavioral-variant or primary progressive aphasia syndromes. Frontal and anterior temporal atrophy on structural imaging supports differential diagnosis from Alzheimer's disease.

name: Dementia with Lewy bodies
overview: An alpha-synuclein-associated dementia characterized by fluctuating cognition, recurrent visual hallucinations, REM-sleep behavior disorder, and parkinsonism. Imaging research emphasizes relative preservation of medial temporal structures compared with Alzheimer's disease.

name: Multiple system atrophy
overview: A rapidly progressive alpha-synucleinopathy combining autonomic failure with parkinsonian or cerebellar features. Imaging research focuses on putaminal, pontine, and cerebellar changes that support differential diagnosis from Parkinson's disease.

name: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
overview: A progressive motor neuron disease affecting upper and lower motor neurons, causing weakness, spasticity, and muscle atrophy; cognitive and behavioral change overlaps with frontotemporal dementia in a subset. Imaging research centers on motor cortex and corticospinal tract degeneration.

name: Parkinson's disease
overview: A progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by bradykinesia, rigidity, and resting tremor, frequently accompanied by non-motor symptoms. Its pathological hallmark is the degeneration of dopaminergic neurons of the substantia nigra with alpha-synuclein pathology; basal ganglia circuits are a major focus of imaging and stimulation research.
